sentences.zh: 輿服四鹵簿附

translations.literal: Carriages and Dress 4, with Supplement on Halberd Guards
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and Dress 4, with Supplement on Halberd Guards

sentences.zh: 皇帝鹵簿太上皇鹵簿皇太子儀衛皇后儀駕太皇太后儀駕皇太后儀駕

translations.literal: The emperor's halberd guard; the retired emperor's halberd guard; the crown prince's ceremonial guard; the empress's ceremonial escort; the grand empress dowager's ceremonial escort; the empress dowager's ceremonial escort
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's Halberd Guard; the Retired Emperor's Halberd Guard; the Crown Prince's Ceremonial Guard; the Empress's Ceremonial Escort; the Grand Empress Dowager's Ceremonial Escort; the Empress Dowager's Ceremonial Escort

sentences.zh: 皇貴妃以下儀仗采仗親王以下儀衛固倫公主以下儀衛

translations.literal: Ceremonial regalia and colored staffs for imperial noble consorts and below; ceremonial guards for princes and below; ceremonial guards for imperial princesses of the first rank and below
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial regalia and colored staffs for imperial noble consorts and below; ceremonial guards for princes and below; ceremonial guards for imperial princesses of the first rank and below

sentences.zh: 額駙儀衛職官儀衛

translations.literal: Ceremonial guards for imperial sons-in-law; ceremonial guards for officials
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards for Imperial Sons-in-Law; Ceremonial Guards for Officials

sentences.zh: 清自太宗天聰六年定儀仗之制，凡國中往來，御前旗三對，傘二柄，校尉六人，其制甚簡。

translations.literal: From the sixth year of Tiancong under Taizong, the Qing fixed regulations for ceremonial regalia. For travel within the realm there were three pairs of imperial front flags, two umbrellas, and six guardsmen—the system was very simple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, in the sixth year of Tiancong, the Qing first set regulations for ceremonial regalia. For journeys within the realm the emperor was preceded by three pairs of imperial flags, two umbrellas, and six guardsmen—a notably spare establishment.

sentences.zh: 自天聰十年改元崇德，始定御仗數目及品官儀從。

translations.literal: From the tenth year of Tiancong, when the era name was changed to Chongde, the numbers of imperial regalia and the ceremonial retinues of ranked officials were first fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tiancong, when the reign title was changed to Chongde, the court first fixed how many pieces of imperial regalia there should be and what ceremonial retinues ranked officials might use.

sentences.zh: 迨世祖入關定鼎，參稽往制，量加增飾。

translations.literal: When the Shizu emperor entered the passes and established the capital, he consulted past regulations and added ornamentation in measured degree.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizu emperor entered the passes and established the dynasty at its new capital, he consulted earlier regulations and added further ornamentation in due measure.

sentences.zh: 原定皇帝儀衛有大駕鹵簿、行駕儀仗、行幸儀仗之別，乾隆十三年，復就原定器數增改釐訂，遂更大駕鹵簿為法駕鹵簿，行駕儀仗為鑾駕鹵簿，行幸儀仗為騎駕鹵簿。

translations.literal: The original regulations for the emperor's ceremonial guard distinguished the Grand Imperial halberd guard, the traveling imperial regalia, and the regalia for imperial progresses. In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, the originally fixed numbers of implements were again increased, revised, and ordered; thereupon the Grand Imperial halberd guard was renamed the Statutory Imperial halberd guard, the traveling imperial regalia became the Imperial Palanquin halberd guard, and the regalia for imperial progresses became the Mounted Imperial halberd guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original regulations the emperor's ceremonial guard was divided into the Grand Imperial halberd guard, traveling imperial regalia, and regalia for imperial progresses. In the thirteenth year of Qianlong the court again revised the originally fixed inventories of equipment and renamed them: the Grand Imperial halberd guard became the Statutory Imperial halberd guard, traveling imperial regalia became the Imperial Palanquin halberd guard, and regalia for imperial progresses became the Mounted Imperial halberd guard.

sentences.zh: 三者合，則為大駕鹵簿。

translations.literal: When the three were combined, they formed the Grand Imperial halberd guard.
translations.idiomatic: Combined, the three constituted the Grand Imperial halberd guard.

sentences.zh: 而凡皇后儀駕、妃嬪儀仗采仗以及親王以下儀衛，均視原定加詳。

translations.literal: As for the empress's ceremonial escort, the ceremonial regalia and colored staffs of consorts, and the ceremonial guards of princes and below, all were made more detailed than the original regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's ceremonial escort, the ceremonial regalia and colored staffs of consorts, and the ceremonial guards of princes and below were all elaborated beyond the original regulations.

sentences.zh: 茲依乾隆朝所定者標目，而以原定器數及崇德初年所定者附見於後。

translations.literal: Here the headings follow what was fixed in the Qianlong reign, while the originally fixed numbers of implements and what was fixed in the early Chongde years are appended afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The headings below follow the Qianlong regulations, with the originally fixed inventories and the early Chongde provisions appended afterward.

sentences.zh: 又太上皇鹵簿、皇太子儀衛，皆一時之制，非同常設，亦並著於篇。

translations.literal: Moreover, the retired emperor's halberd guard and the crown prince's ceremonial guard were both temporary institutions, not regularly established, and are also recorded in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor's halberd guard and the crown prince's ceremonial guard were likewise included, though both were temporary arrangements rather than standing institutions.

sentences.zh: 庶考因革者，得以沿流溯源，詳稽一代之制焉。

translations.literal: Thus those who examine change and continuity may follow the current downstream to its source and scrutinize in detail the regulations of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Readers tracing institutional change may thus follow the stream to its source and examine in detail how the dynasty's ceremonial system took shape.

sentences.zh: 皇帝大駕鹵簿，圜丘、祈穀、常雩三大祀用之。

translations.literal: The emperor's Grand Imperial halberd guard was used for the three great sacrifices at the Circular Mound, for prayer for grain, and for the regular rain sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's Grand Imperial halberd guard was employed for the three great sacrifices at the Circular Mound, for prayer for grain, and for the regular rain sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 大閱時詣行宮，禮成還宮，亦用之。

translations.literal: When proceeding to the traveling palace during a grand review, and when returning to the palace after the rites were completed, it was also used.
translations.idiomatic: It was also used when the emperor went to the traveling palace for a grand military review and when he returned to the palace after the rites were concluded.

sentences.zh: 其制，前列導象四，次寶象五，次靜鞭四。

translations.literal: Its arrangement: first came four guide elephants; next five treasure elephants; next four silent whips.
translations.idiomatic: Its order of march placed four guide elephants in the van, followed by five treasure elephants and four silent whips.

sentences.zh: 次前部大樂，其器大銅角四，小銅角四，金口角四。

translations.literal: Next came the front-section grand music, its instruments being four large bronze horns, four small bronze horns, and four gilt bronze mouth-horns.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the front-section grand music, with four large bronze horns, four small bronze horns, and four gilt bronze mouth-horns.

sentences.zh: 次革輅駕馬四，木輅駕馬六，象輅駕馬八，金輅駕象一，玉輅駕象一。

translations.literal: Next the leather chariot drawn by four horses, the wooden chariot drawn by six horses, the elephant chariot drawn by eight horses, the gold chariot drawn by one elephant, and the jade chariot drawn by one elephant.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the five ceremonial chariots: the leather chariot with four horses, the wooden chariot with six, the elephant chariot with eight, the gold chariot with one elephant, and the jade chariot with one elephant.

sentences.zh: 次鐃歌樂，鐃歌鼓吹與行幸樂並設，名鐃歌樂。

translations.literal: Next the naoge music; naoge drum-and-blow music and progress music were both set out together and called naoge music.
translations.idiomatic: Next came naoge music—the naoge drum-and-blow ensemble and progress music were deployed together under that single name.

sentences.zh: 其器金二，銅鼓四，銅鈸二，扁鼓二，銅點二，龍篴二，平篴二，雲鑼二，管二，笙二，金口角八，大銅角十六，小銅角十六，蒙古角二，金鉦四，畫角二十四，龍鼓二十四，龍篴十二，拍板四，仗鼓四，金四，龍鼓二十四，間以紅鐙六。

translations.literal: Its instruments: two gongs; four bronze drums; two bronze cymbals; two flat drums; two bronze clappers; two dragon flutes; two level flutes; two cloud gongs; two pipes; two sheng; eight gilt bronze mouth-horns; sixteen large bronze horns; sixteen small bronze horns; two Mongol horns; four gilt cymbals; twenty-four painted horns; twenty-four dragon drums; twelve dragon flutes; four clappers; four guard drums; four gongs; twenty-four dragon drums, interspersed with six red lanterns.
translations.idiomatic: Its instruments comprised two gongs, four bronze drums, two bronze cymbals, two flat drums, two bronze clappers, two dragon flutes, two level flutes, two cloud gongs, two pipes, two sheng, eight gilt bronze mouth-horns, sixteen large and sixteen small bronze horns, two Mongol horns, four gilt cymbals, twenty-four painted horns, twenty-four dragon drums, twelve dragon flutes, four clappers, four guard drums, four additional gongs, another twenty-four dragon drums, and six red lanterns interspersed among them.

sentences.zh: 次引仗六，御仗十六，吾仗十六，立瓜、臥瓜各十六，星、鉞各十六，出警、入蹕旗各一，五色金龍小旗四十，次翠華旗二，金鼓旗二，門旗八，日、月旗各一，五雲旗五，五雷旗五，八風旗八，甘雨旗四，列宿旗二十八，五星旗五，五嶽旗五，四瀆旗四，神武、硃雀、青龍、白虎旗各一，天馬、天鹿、辟邪、犀牛、赤熊、黃羆、白澤、角端、游麟、彩獅、振鷺、鳴鳶、赤烏、華蟲、黃鵠、白雉、雲鶴、孔雀、儀鳳、翔鸞旗各一。

translations.literal: Next six guide staffs, sixteen imperial staffs, sixteen wu staffs, sixteen standing-melon and sixteen reclining-melon [weapons], sixteen star-emblems and sixteen battle-axes, one each of the exit-guard and enter-forbidden-zone flags, forty small five-colored golden-dragon flags; next two emerald-splendor flags, two golden-drum flags, eight gate flags, one each of sun and moon flags, five five-cloud flags, five five-thunder flags, eight eight-wind flags, four sweet-rain flags, twenty-eight lodge flags, five five-star flags, five five-mountain flags, four four-river flags, one each of the Divine Martial, Vermilion Bird, Azure Dragon, and White Tiger flags, and one each of the heavenly horse, heavenly deer, ward-off-evil, rhinoceros, red bear, yellow bear, white marsh-beast, horned tip, roaming qilin, colored lion, vibrating egret, crying kite, red crow, patterned insect, yellow swan-goose, white pheasant, cloud crane, peacock, ceremonial phoenix, and soaring luan flags.
translations.idiomatic: Next came six guide staffs, sixteen imperial staffs, sixteen wu staffs, sixteen standing-melon and sixteen reclining-melon emblems, sixteen star-maces and sixteen battle-axes, one exit-guard flag and one enter-forbidden-zone flag, and forty small five-colored golden-dragon flags; then two emerald-splendor flags, two golden-drum flags, eight gate flags, the sun and moon flags, five-cloud flags, five-thunder flags, eight-wind flags, four sweet-rain flags, twenty-eight constellation flags, five planetary flags, five sacred-mountain flags, four great-river flags, the Divine Martial, Vermilion Bird, Azure Dragon, and White Tiger flags, and one each of the heavenly horse, heavenly deer, ward-off-evil, rhinoceros, red bear, yellow bear, white marsh-beast, horned tip, roaming qilin, colored lion, vibrating egret, crying kite, red crow, patterned insect, yellow swan-goose, white pheasant, cloud crane, peacock, ceremonial phoenix, and soaring luan flags.

sentences.zh: 五色龍纛四十，前鋒纛八，護軍纛八，驍騎纛二十四。

translations.literal: Forty five-colored dragon banners, eight vanguard banners, eight guard-army banners, and twenty-four bold-cavalry banners.
translations.idiomatic: Forty five-colored dragon banners followed, with eight vanguard banners, eight guard-army banners, and twenty-four bold-cavalry banners.

sentences.zh: 次黃麾四，儀鍠氅四，金節四，進善納言、敷文振武、褒功懷遠、行慶施惠、明刑弼教、教孝表節旌各二。

translations.literal: Next four yellow command banners, four ceremonial gong-canopies, four golden staffs of office, and two each of the banners for receiving good counsel, spreading culture and invigorating arms, praising merit and cherishing the distant, bestowing celebration and extending grace, clarifying punishments and assisting instruction, and teaching filial piety and displaying integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Next came four yellow command banners, four ceremonial gong-canopies, four golden staffs of office, and two each of the banners bearing the slogans for receiving good counsel, spreading culture and invigorating arms, praising merit and cherishing the distant, bestowing celebration and extending grace, clarifying punishments and assisting instruction, and teaching filial piety and displaying integrity.

sentences.zh: 龍頭幡四，豹尾幡四，絳引幡四，信幡四。

translations.literal: Four dragon-head banners, four leopard-tail banners, four crimson guide banners, and four trust banners.
translations.idiomatic: Four dragon-head banners, four leopard-tail banners, four crimson guide banners, and four trust banners followed.

sentences.zh: 羽葆幢四，霓幢四，紫幢四，長壽幢四。

translations.literal: Four feather-canopy banners, four rainbow banners, four purple banners, and four longevity banners.
translations.idiomatic: Four feather-canopy banners, four rainbow banners, four purple banners, and four longevity banners came next.

sentences.zh: 次鸞鳳赤方扇八，雉尾扇八，孔雀扇八，單龍赤團扇八，單龍黃團扇八，雙龍赤團扇八，雙龍黃團扇八，赤滿單龍團扇六，黃滿雙龍團扇六，壽字黃扇八。

translations.literal: Next eight square luan-phoenix red fans, eight pheasant-tail fans, eight peacock fans, eight single-dragon red round fans, eight single-dragon yellow round fans, eight double-dragon red round fans, eight double-dragon yellow round fans, six red full single-dragon round fans, six yellow full double-dragon round fans, and eight yellow fans bearing the character for longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Next came eight square luan-phoenix red fans, eight pheasant-tail fans, eight peacock fans, eight single-dragon red round fans, eight single-dragon yellow round fans, eight double-dragon red round fans, eight double-dragon yellow round fans, six red full single-dragon round fans, six yellow full double-dragon round fans, and eight yellow fans emblazoned with the character for longevity.

sentences.zh: 次赤素方傘四，紫素方傘四，五色花傘十，五色妝緞傘十，間以五色九龍團傘十。

translations.literal: Next four plain red square umbrellas, four plain purple square umbrellas, ten five-colored floral umbrellas, ten five-colored figured-satin umbrellas, interspersed with ten five-colored nine-dragon round umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: Next came four plain red square umbrellas, four plain purple square umbrellas, ten five-colored floral umbrellas, ten five-colored figured-satin umbrellas, and ten five-colored nine-dragon round umbrellas interspersed among them.

sentences.zh: 次九龍黃蓋二十，紫芝蓋二，翠華蓋二，九龍曲柄黃蓋四。

translations.literal: Next twenty yellow nine-dragon canopies, two purple lingzhi canopies, two emerald-splendor canopies, and four curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopies.
translations.idiomatic: Next came twenty yellow nine-dragon canopies, two purple lingzhi canopies, two emerald-splendor canopies, and four curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopies.

sentences.zh: 次戟四，殳四，豹尾槍三十，弓矢三十，儀刀三十。

translations.literal: Next four halberds, four shu [ceremonial staffs], thirty leopard-tail spears, thirty bows and arrows, and thirty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Next came four halberds, four ceremonial staffs, thirty leopard-tail spears, thirty bows and arrows, and thirty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 次仗馬十。

translations.literal: Next ten ceremonial horses.
translations.idiomatic: Next came ten ceremonial horses.

sentences.zh: 次金方几一，金交椅一，金瓶二，金盥盤一，金盂一，金盒二，金爐二，拂二。

translations.literal: Next one square golden table, one golden armchair, two golden vases, one golden wash-basin, one golden bowl, two golden boxes, two golden censers, and two fly-whisks.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one square golden table, one golden armchair, two golden vases, one golden wash-basin, one golden bowl, two golden boxes, two golden censers, and two fly-whisks.

sentences.zh: 次九龍曲柄黃蓋一。

translations.literal: Next one curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopy.

sentences.zh: 前引佩刀大臣十人，提爐二，玉輦在中。

translations.literal: Ten sword-bearing ministers led in front, two incense-bearers, and the jade imperial carriage in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Ten sword-bearing ministers led in front, two attendants carried censers, and the jade imperial carriage rode at the center.

sentences.zh: 後扈佩刀大臣二人，豹尾班執槍佩儀刀侍衛各十人，佩弓矢侍衛二十人，領侍衛內大臣一人，侍衛班領二人。

translations.literal: Two sword-bearing ministers guarded the rear; the leopard-tail company had ten guards each bearing spears and ceremonial swords, and twenty guards bearing bows and arrows; one chief grand guard of the inner service, and two guard company leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Two sword-bearing ministers brought up the rear; the leopard-tail company comprised ten guards with spears and ten with ceremonial swords, while twenty guards bore bows and arrows; a chief grand guard of the inner service and two guard company leaders completed the escort.

sentences.zh: 後管宗人府王、公二人，散秩大臣一人，前鋒護軍統領一人，給事中、御史二人，各部郎中、員外郎四人，侍衛班領一人，署侍衛班領一人，侍衛什長二人。

translations.literal: Following them were two princes and dukes from the Imperial Clan Court, one minister without regular portfolio, one commander of vanguard and guard armies, two supervising secretaries and censors, four department directors and vice directors, one guard company leader, one acting guard company leader, and two guard squad chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Behind them followed two princes and dukes from the Imperial Clan Court, a minister without regular portfolio, the commander of vanguard and guard armies, two supervising secretaries and censors, four department directors and vice directors, a guard company leader, an acting guard company leader, and two guard squad chiefs.

sentences.zh: 次黃龍大纛二，領侍衛內大臣一人，司纛侍衛什長二人，建纛親軍四人，鳴佩螺親軍六人。

translations.literal: Next two great yellow-dragon banners; one chief grand guard of the inner service, two guard squad chiefs in charge of banners, four personal guards who raised the banners, and six personal guards who sounded conch shells.
translations.idiomatic: The procession closed with two great yellow-dragon banners, attended by a chief grand guard of the inner service, two guard squad chiefs in charge of banners, four personal guards who raised the banners, and six personal guards who sounded conch shells.

sentences.zh: 太宗崇德元年，備大駕鹵簿，玉璽四顆。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde under Taizong, the Grand Imperial halberd guard was prepared, with four jade seals.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's first Chongde year the court prepared the Grand Imperial halberd guard, including four jade seals.

sentences.zh: 黃傘五，團扇二。

translations.literal: Five yellow umbrellas and two round fans.
translations.idiomatic: There were five yellow umbrellas and two round fans.

sentences.zh: 纛十，旗十。

translations.literal: Ten great banners and ten flags.
translations.idiomatic: Ten great banners and ten flags were provided.

sentences.zh: 大刀六，戟六。

translations.literal: Six great swords and six halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Six great swords and six halberds were included.

sentences.zh: 立瓜、臥瓜、骨朵各二，吾仗六。

translations.literal: Two each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, and mace; six wu staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Two each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, and mace emblems, plus six wu staffs.

sentences.zh: 馬十。

translations.literal: Ten horses.
translations.idiomatic: Ten ceremonial horses were provided.

sentences.zh: 金椅、金杌、香盒、香爐、金水盆、金唾壺、金瓶、樂器全設。

translations.literal: Golden chair, golden stool, incense box, incense burner, golden water basin, golden spittoon, golden vase, and the full set of musical instruments were all provided.
translations.idiomatic: A golden chair, golden stool, incense box, incense burner, golden water basin, golden spittoon, golden vase, and the full complement of musical instruments were all provided.

sentences.zh: 嗣復定儀仗數目，用金漆椅一，金漆杌一，蠅拂四，金唾盂一，金壺一，金瓶、金盆各一，香爐、香盒各二。

translations.literal: Later the numbers of ceremonial regalia were again fixed: one gilt chair, one gilt stool, four fly-whisks, one golden spittoon-bowl, one golden ewer, one golden vase and one golden basin each, and two incense burners and two incense boxes each.
translations.idiomatic: The court later revised the inventory again: one gilt chair, one gilt stool, four fly-whisks, one golden spittoon-bowl, one golden ewer, one golden vase, one golden basin, and two each of incense burners and incense boxes.

sentences.zh: 曲柄傘一，直柄傘四，扇二，節四。

translations.literal: One curved-handle umbrella, four straight-handle umbrellas, two fans, and four staffs of office.
translations.idiomatic: One curved-handle umbrella, four straight-handle umbrellas, two fans, and four staffs of office were specified.

sentences.zh: 骨朵二，立瓜、臥瓜各二，吾仗六，紅仗四。

translations.literal: Two maces, two each of standing-melon and reclining-melon, six wu staffs, and four red staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Two maces, two each of standing-melon and reclining-melon emblems, six wu staffs, and four red staffs were added.

sentences.zh: 鑼二，鼓二，畫角四，簫二，笙二，架鼓四，橫笛二，龍頭橫笛二，檀板二，小銅鈸四，小銅鑼二，大銅鑼四，雲鑼二，鎖吶四。

translations.literal: Two gongs, two drums, four painted horns, two xiao, two sheng, four frame drums, two transverse flutes, two dragon-head transverse flutes, two clapper boards, four small bronze cymbals, two small bronze gongs, four large bronze gongs, two cloud gongs, and four suona.
translations.idiomatic: Musical equipment comprised two gongs, two drums, four painted horns, two xiao, two sheng, four frame drums, two transverse flutes, two dragon-head transverse flutes, two clapper boards, four small bronze cymbals, two small bronze gongs, four large bronze gongs, two cloud gongs, and four suona.

sentences.zh: 世祖入關，一仍舊制。

translations.literal: When the Shizu emperor entered the passes, the old system was retained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu emperor entered the passes, the court kept the old system unchanged.

sentences.zh: 迨順治三年以後，更定皇帝鹵簿，有大駕鹵簿、行駕儀仗、行幸儀仗之別。

translations.literal: From the third year of Shunzhi onward, the emperor's halberd guard was revised, with distinctions among the Grand Imperial halberd guard, traveling imperial regalia, and regalia for imperial progresses.
translations.idiomatic: From the third year of Shunzhi onward the emperor's halberd guard was reorganized into the Grand Imperial halberd guard, traveling imperial regalia, and regalia for imperial progresses.

sentences.zh: 大駕鹵簿之制，曲柄九，龍傘四，直柄九龍傘十六，直柄瑞草傘六，直柄花傘六，方傘八。

translations.literal: The regulations for the Grand Imperial halberd guard: nine curved-handle [canopies], four dragon umbrellas, sixteen straight-handle nine-dragon umbrellas, six straight-handle auspicious-grass umbrellas, six straight-handle floral umbrellas, and eight square umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Grand Imperial halberd guard there were nine curved-handle canopies, four dragon umbrellas, sixteen straight-handle nine-dragon umbrellas, six straight-handle auspicious-grass umbrellas, six straight-handle floral umbrellas, and eight square umbrellas.

sentences.zh: 大刀二十，弓矢二十，豹尾槍二十，龍頭方天戟四。

translations.literal: Twenty great swords, twenty bows and arrows, twenty leopard-tail spears, and four dragon-head square-heaven halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty great swords, twenty bows and arrows, twenty leopard-tail spears, and four dragon-head square-heaven halberds were specified.

sentences.zh: 黃麾二，絳引幡四，信幡、傳教幡、告止幡、政平訟理幡各四，儀鍠氅八，羽葆幢四，青龍、白虎、硃雀、神武幢各一，豹尾幡、龍頭竿幡各四。

translations.literal: Two yellow command banners, four crimson guide banners, four each of trust, teaching, stop-proclamation, and government-in-order banners, eight ceremonial gong-canopies, four feather-canopy banners, one each of Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, and Divine Martial banners, and four each of leopard-tail and dragon-pole banners.
translations.idiomatic: Two yellow command banners, four crimson guide banners, four each of the trust, teaching, stop-proclamation, and government-in-order banners, eight ceremonial gong-canopies, four feather-canopy banners, the Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, and Divine Martial banners, and four each of leopard-tail and dragon-pole banners were included.

sentences.zh: 金節四。

translations.literal: Four golden staffs of office.
translations.idiomatic: Four golden staffs of office were provided.

sentences.zh: 銷金龍纛、銷金龍小旗各二十。

translations.literal: Twenty gilded-dragon great banners and twenty gilded-dragon small flags.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty gilded-dragon great banners and twenty gilded-dragon small flags were specified.

sentences.zh: 金鉞六。

translations.literal: Six golden battle-axes.
translations.idiomatic: Six golden battle-axes were included.

sentences.zh: 馬十。

translations.literal: Ten horses.
translations.idiomatic: Ten ceremonial horses were provided.

sentences.zh: 鸞鳳扇八，單龍扇十二，雙龍扇二十。

translations.literal: Eight luan-phoenix fans, twelve single-dragon fans, and twenty double-dragon fans.
translations.idiomatic: Eight luan-phoenix fans, twelve single-dragon fans, and twenty double-dragon fans were specified.

sentences.zh: 拂子二，紅鐙六，金香爐、金瓶、金香盒各二，金唾壺、金盆、金杌、金交椅、金腳踏各一。

translations.literal: Two fly-whisks, six red lanterns, two each of golden incense burners, golden vases, and golden incense boxes, and one each of golden spittoon, golden basin, golden stool, golden armchair, and golden footrest.
translations.idiomatic: Two fly-whisks, six red lanterns, two each of golden incense burners, vases, and incense boxes, and one each of golden spittoon, basin, stool, armchair, and footrest were provided.

sentences.zh: 御仗六，星六。

translations.literal: Six imperial staffs and six star-emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Six imperial staffs and six star-emblems were included.

sentences.zh: 篦頭八。

translations.literal: Eight comb-heads.
translations.idiomatic: Eight comb-head emblems were specified.

sentences.zh: 棕薦三十。

translations.literal: Thirty palm-fiber mats.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty palm-fiber mats were provided.

sentences.zh: 靜鞭三十。

translations.literal: Thirty silent whips.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty silent whips were included.

sentences.zh: 品級山七十二。

translations.literal: Seventy-two rank-indicator screens.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two rank-indicator screens were deployed.

sentences.zh: 肅靜旗、金鼓旗、白澤旗各二，門旗八，日、月、風、雲、雷、雨旗各一，五緯旗五，二十八宿旗各一，北斗旗一，五嶽旗五，四瀆旗四，青龍、白虎、硃雀、神武、天鹿、天馬、鸞麟、熊羆旗各一。

translations.literal: Two each of the silence, golden-drum, and white marsh-beast flags; eight gate flags; one each of sun, moon, wind, cloud, thunder, and rain flags; five five-planet flags; one each of the twenty-eight lodge flags; one Big Dipper flag; five five-mountain flags; four four-river flags; and one each of the Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, Divine Martial, heavenly deer, heavenly horse, luan-qilin, and bear flags.
translations.idiomatic: Two each of the silence, golden-drum, and white marsh-beast flags were set out, with eight gate flags, the sun, moon, wind, cloud, thunder, and rain flags, five planetary flags, the twenty-eight constellation flags, one Big Dipper flag, five sacred-mountain flags, four great-river flags, and the Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, Divine Martial, heavenly deer, heavenly horse, luan-qilin, and bear flags.

sentences.zh: 立瓜、臥瓜、吾仗各六。

translations.literal: Six each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, and wu staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Six each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, and wu staffs were provided.

sentences.zh: 畫角二十四，鼓四十八，大銅號、小銅號各八，金、金鉦、仗鼓各四，龍頭笛十二，板四串。

translations.literal: Twenty-four painted horns, forty-eight drums, eight each of large and small bronze horns, four each of gongs, gilt cymbals, and guard drums, twelve dragon-head flutes, and four strings of clappers.
translations.idiomatic: Musical equipment comprised twenty-four painted horns, forty-eight drums, eight large and eight small bronze horns, four each of gongs, gilt cymbals, and guard drums, twelve dragon-head flutes, and four strings of clappers.

sentences.zh: 凡郊祀大典，萬壽、元旦、冬至三大朝會及諸典禮皆用之。

translations.literal: It was used for all suburban sacrifice grand ceremonies, the three great court assemblies of Longevity, New Year's Day, and Winter Solstice, and all other ritual occasions.
translations.idiomatic: It was employed for suburban sacrifice grand ceremonies, the three great court assemblies of Longevity, New Year's Day, and Winter Solstice, and all other state rituals.

sentences.zh: 法駕鹵簿，與大駕鹵簿同，惟彼用鐃歌樂，此則用鐃歌鼓吹。

translations.literal: The Statutory Imperial halberd guard was the same as the Grand Imperial halberd guard, except that the latter used naoge music while this used naoge drum-and-blow.
translations.idiomatic: The Statutory Imperial halberd guard matched the Grand Imperial guard in most respects, but where the Grand Imperial array used naoge music, the Statutory array used naoge drum-and-blow.

sentences.zh: 其器大銅角八，小銅角八，金鉦四，畫角二十四，龍鼓二十四，龍篴十二，拍板四，仗鼓四，金二，龍鼓二十四，間以紅鐙六，視鐃歌樂為減。

translations.literal: Its instruments: eight large bronze horns, eight small bronze horns, four gilt cymbals, twenty-four painted horns, twenty-four dragon drums, twelve dragon flutes, four clappers, four guard drums, two gongs, twenty-four dragon drums interspersed with six red lanterns—a reduction compared with naoge music.
translations.idiomatic: Its instruments comprised eight large and eight small bronze horns, four gilt cymbals, twenty-four painted horns, twenty-four dragon drums, twelve dragon flutes, four clappers, four guard drums, two gongs, another twenty-four dragon drums, and six red lanterns interspersed among them—a lighter ensemble than full naoge music.

sentences.zh: 又御仗、吾仗、立瓜、臥瓜、星、鉞皆各六，五色金龍小旗二十，五色龍纛二十，九龍黃蓋十，豹尾槍二十，弓矢二十，儀刀二十，佩弓矢侍衛十人，其赤滿單龍團扇、黃滿雙龍團扇及五色妝緞傘皆不設，亦均較大駕為減。

translations.literal: Moreover, imperial staffs, wu staffs, standing-melon, reclining-melon, star-emblems, and battle-axes were six each; twenty small five-colored golden-dragon flags; twenty five-colored dragon banners; ten yellow nine-dragon canopies; twenty leopard-tail spears; twenty bows and arrows; twenty ceremonial swords; ten guards bearing bows and arrows; the red full single-dragon round fans, yellow full double-dragon round fans, and five-colored figured-satin umbrellas were not set out—all reduced compared with the Grand Imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial staffs, wu staffs, standing-melon and reclining-melon emblems, star-maces, and battle-axes were limited to six each; there were twenty small five-colored golden-dragon flags, twenty five-colored dragon banners, ten yellow nine-dragon canopies, twenty leopard-tail spears, twenty bows and arrows, twenty ceremonial swords, and ten guards bearing bows and arrows. The red full single-dragon round fans, yellow full double-dragon round fans, and five-colored figured-satin umbrellas were omitted—every category reduced from the Grand Imperial establishment.

sentences.zh: 又玉輦改設金輦，餘均與大駕鹵簿同。

translations.literal: Moreover, the jade imperial carriage was replaced by the gold imperial carriage; the rest was the same as the Grand Imperial halberd guard.
translations.idiomatic: The jade imperial carriage was replaced by the gold carriage; otherwise the array matched the Grand Imperial halberd guard.

sentences.zh: 凡祭方澤、太廟、社稷、日月、先農各壇，歷代帝王、先師各廟，則陳之。

translations.literal: It was arrayed for sacrifices at the Square Mound, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the altars of soil and grain, sun and moon, and the First Farmer, and at the temples of successive emperors and the First Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: It was deployed for sacrifices at the Square Mound, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the altars of soil and grain, sun and moon, and the First Farmer, and at the temples of successive emperors and the First Teacher.

sentences.zh: 若遇慶典朝賀，則陳於太和殿庭。

translations.literal: When celebratory court congratulations occurred, it was arrayed in the courtyard of the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: For celebratory court congratulations it was arrayed in the courtyard of the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 其制，九龍曲柄黃華蓋設於太和殿門外正中，次拂、爐、盒、盂、盤、瓶、椅、幾在殿檐東、西。

translations.literal: Its arrangement: the curved-handle yellow nine-dragon splendor canopy was set at the center outside the gate of the Hall of Supreme Harmony; next, fly-whisks, censers, boxes, bowls, basins, vases, chairs, and tables were placed east and west under the eaves.
translations.idiomatic: The curved-handle yellow nine-dragon splendor canopy stood at the center outside the Hall of Supreme Harmony, with fly-whisks, censers, boxes, bowls, basins, vases, chairs, and tables arranged east and west beneath the eaves.

sentences.zh: 次儀刀、弓矢、豹尾槍親軍、護軍相間為十班，暨殳戟，均在丹陛東、西。

translations.literal: Next ceremonial swords, bows and arrows, and leopard-tail spears were alternated in ten companies of personal guards and guard troops, together with shu and halberds, all on the east and west of the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial swords, bows and arrows, and leopard-tail spears were alternated in ten companies of personal and guard troops, with ceremonial staffs and halberds, all arrayed east and west on the red steps.

sentences.zh: 次九龍曲柄黃蓋、翠華蓋、紫芝蓋、九龍黃蓋、五色九龍傘、五色花傘，自丹陛三成，相間達於兩階。

translations.literal: Next curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopies, emerald-splendor canopies, purple lingzhi canopies, yellow nine-dragon canopies, five-colored nine-dragon umbrellas, and five-colored floral umbrellas, starting from the third tier of the red steps, were alternately arrayed reaching the two flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: Curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopies, emerald-splendor canopies, purple lingzhi canopies, yellow nine-dragon canopies, five-colored nine-dragon umbrellas, and five-colored floral umbrellas were alternately arrayed from the third tier of the red steps down to the lower flights.

sentences.zh: 階下靜鞭、仗馬列甬道東、西。

translations.literal: Below the steps, silent whips and ceremonial horses were lined east and west along the central passage.
translations.idiomatic: Silent whips and ceremonial horses lined the central passage east and west below the steps.

sentences.zh: 紫、赤方傘、扇，幢、幡、旌、節、氅、麾、纛、旗、鉞、星、瓜、仗，列丹墀東、西。

translations.literal: Purple and red square umbrellas, fans, banners, pennants, flags, staffs of office, canopies, command banners, great banners, flags, battle-axes, star-emblems, melon [weapons], and staffs were arrayed east and west on the red courtyard pavement.
translations.idiomatic: Purple and red square umbrellas, fans, banners, pennants, flags, staffs of office, canopies, command banners, great banners, battle-axes, star-emblems, melon emblems, and ceremonial staffs were arrayed east and west on the red courtyard pavement.

sentences.zh: 玉輦、金輦在太和門外，五輅在午門外，寶象在五輅之南，鹵簿樂即鐃歌鼓吹。

translations.literal: The jade and gold imperial carriages were outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony; the five ceremonial chariots were outside the Meridian Gate; treasure elephants were south of the five chariots; halberd-guard music was naoge drum-and-blow.
translations.idiomatic: The jade and gold imperial carriages stood outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, the five ceremonial chariots outside the Meridian Gate, and treasure elephants south of the chariots, with naoge drum-and-blow as the halberd-guard music.

sentences.zh: 在寶象之南，朝象即導象。

translations.literal: South of the treasure elephants, the court elephants were the guide elephants.
translations.idiomatic: South of the treasure elephants stood the court elephants, which served as guide elephants.

sentences.zh: 在天安門外。

translations.literal: This was outside the Gate of Heavenly Peace.
translations.idiomatic: These were stationed outside the Gate of Heavenly Peace.

sentences.zh: 若於圓明園行慶賀禮，則陳於正大光明殿階下，至大宮門外，惟輦輅儀象不設。

translations.literal: If celebratory rites were performed at the Old Summer Palace, the array was set below the steps of the Hall of Imperial Splendor up to outside the Great Palace Gate, but imperial carriages, chariots, and ceremonial elephants were not set out.
translations.idiomatic: When celebratory rites were held at the Old Summer Palace, the array ran from below the Hall of Imperial Splendor to the Great Palace Gate, though imperial carriages, chariots, and ceremonial elephants were omitted.

sentences.zh: 若御樓受俘，則設九龍曲柄黃華蓋於樓檐下，設丹陛鹵簿於午門外左右兩觀下，設丹墀鹵簿於闕左右門至端門北，設仗馬於兩角樓前，設輦輅儀象於天安門外，設靜鞭於兩角樓夾御道左右，設金鼓鐃歌大樂鐃歌鼓吹與前部大樂並列，曰金鼓鐃歌大樂。

translations.literal: If the emperor received captives from the tower, the curved-handle yellow nine-dragon splendor canopy was set beneath the eaves; red-step halberd guards were set beneath the left and right watch-towers outside the Meridian Gate; red-courtyard halberd guards were set from the left and right gate-towers to north of the End Gate; ceremonial horses were set before the two corner towers; carriages, chariots, and ceremonial elephants were set outside the Gate of Heavenly Peace; silent whips were set on either side of the imperial roadway between the corner towers; golden-drum naoge grand music, naoge drum-and-blow, and front-section grand music were arrayed together and called golden-drum naoge grand music.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received captives from the tower, the curved-handle yellow nine-dragon splendor canopy was placed beneath the eaves; red-step halberd guards beneath the watch-towers outside the Meridian Gate; red-courtyard halberd guards from the gate-towers to the End Gate; ceremonial horses before the corner towers; carriages, chariots, and elephants outside the Gate of Heavenly Peace; silent whips flanking the imperial roadway between the corner towers; and golden-drum naoge grand music, naoge drum-and-blow, and front-section grand music arrayed together as golden-drum naoge grand music.

sentences.zh: 於午門前。

translations.literal: This was before the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: This ensemble stood before the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 設丹陛大樂於鹵簿之末，其器雲鑼二，方響二，簫二，篴四，頭管四，笙四，大鼓二，仗鼓一，拍板一。

translations.literal: Red-step grand music was set at the end of the halberd guard; its instruments were two cloud gongs, two square chimes, two xiao, four di, four lead pipes, four sheng, two large drums, one guard drum, and one clapper.
translations.idiomatic: Red-step grand music closed the halberd-guard array, with two cloud gongs, two square chimes, two xiao, four di, four lead pipes, four sheng, two large drums, one guard drum, and one clapper.

sentences.zh: 鑾駕鹵簿，行幸於皇城則陳之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Palanquin halberd guard was arrayed when the emperor progressed within the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Palanquin halberd guard was deployed when the emperor traveled within the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 其制，前列導迎樂，先以戲竹二，次管六，篴四，笙二，雲鑼二，導迎鼓一，拍板一。

translations.literal: Its arrangement: first came guide-and-welcome music, beginning with two theatrical bamboo [clappers], then six pipes, four di, two sheng, two cloud gongs, one guide-and-welcome drum, and one clapper.
translations.idiomatic: It opened with guide-and-welcome music: two theatrical bamboo clappers, then six pipes, four di, two sheng, two cloud gongs, one guide-and-welcome drum, and one clapper.

sentences.zh: 次御仗四，吾仗四，立瓜、臥瓜、星、鉞各四，次五色金龍小旗十，五色龍纛十。

translations.literal: Next four imperial staffs, four wu staffs, four each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, star-emblems, and battle-axes; next ten small five-colored golden-dragon flags and ten five-colored dragon banners.
translations.idiomatic: Next came four imperial staffs, four wu staffs, four each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, star-maces, and battle-axes, then ten small five-colored golden-dragon flags and ten five-colored dragon banners.

sentences.zh: 次雙龍黃團扇十，黃九龍傘十。

translations.literal: Next ten double-dragon yellow round fans and ten yellow nine-dragon umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: Ten double-dragon yellow round fans and ten yellow nine-dragon umbrellas followed.

sentences.zh: 次九龍曲柄黃華蓋一。

translations.literal: Next one curved-handle yellow nine-dragon splendor canopy.
translations.idiomatic: One curved-handle yellow nine-dragon splendor canopy came next.

sentences.zh: 皆在皇帝步輦前。

translations.literal: All were before the emperor's walking palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: All of these preceded the emperor's walking palanquin.

sentences.zh: 次前引佩刀大臣十人，後扈佩刀大臣二人，步輦在中，次豹尾班侍衛執槍十人，佩儀刀十人，佩弓矢十人，殿以黃龍大纛。

translations.literal: Next ten sword-bearing ministers led in front, two sword-bearing ministers guarded the rear, the walking palanquin was in the center; next the leopard-tail company had ten guards bearing spears, ten bearing ceremonial swords, and ten bearing bows and arrows, closed by the great yellow-dragon banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ten sword-bearing ministers led in front and two brought up the rear, with the walking palanquin at the center; the leopard-tail company comprised ten guards with spears, ten with ceremonial swords, and ten with bows and arrows, closed by the great yellow-dragon banner.

sentences.zh: 原定行駕儀仗，銷金九龍傘十，銷金龍纛十，銷金龍小旗十，雙龍扇十。

translations.literal: Under the original traveling imperial regalia: ten gilded nine-dragon umbrellas, ten gilded dragon banners, ten gilded dragon small flags, and ten double-dragon fans.
translations.idiomatic: The original traveling imperial regalia comprised ten gilded nine-dragon umbrellas, ten gilded dragon banners, ten gilded dragon small flags, and ten double-dragon fans.

sentences.zh: 金鉞四，星四，御仗四，吾仗四，立瓜、臥瓜各四。

translations.literal: Four golden battle-axes, four star-emblems, four imperial staffs, four wu staffs, and four each of standing-melon and reclining-melon.
translations.idiomatic: Four golden battle-axes, four star-emblems, four imperial staffs, four wu staffs, and four each of standing-melon and reclining-melon emblems were specified.

sentences.zh: 凡車駕出入，執事人馬上排列。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage went out or in, the attendants were arrayed on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial carriage entered or left, attendants were arrayed on horseback.

sentences.zh: 騎駕鹵簿，巡方若大閱則陳之。

translations.literal: The Mounted Imperial halberd guard was arrayed for tours of the realm or grand military reviews.
translations.idiomatic: The Mounted Imperial halberd guard was deployed for imperial tours and grand military reviews.

sentences.zh: 其制，前列鐃歌大樂。

translations.literal: Its arrangement: naoge grand music led in front.
translations.idiomatic: It opened with naoge grand music at the head of the column.

sentences.zh: 間以鐃歌清樂，器用大銅角八，小銅角八，金口角八，雲鑼二，龍篴二，平篴二，管二，笙二，銅鼓四，金二，銅點二，銅鈸二，行鼓二，蒙古角二。

translations.literal: Interspersed with naoge clear music; its instruments were eight large bronze horns, eight small bronze horns, eight gilt bronze mouth-horns, two cloud gongs, two dragon flutes, two level flutes, two pipes, two sheng, four bronze drums, two gongs, two bronze clappers, two bronze cymbals, two marching drums, and two Mongol horns.
translations.idiomatic: Naoge clear music was interspersed among them, with eight large and eight small bronze horns, eight gilt bronze mouth-horns, two cloud gongs, two dragon flutes, two level flutes, two pipes, two sheng, four bronze drums, two gongs, two bronze clappers, two bronze cymbals, two marching drums, and two Mongol horns.

sentences.zh: 次御仗六，吾仗六，立瓜、臥瓜、星、鉞各六。

translations.literal: Next six imperial staffs, six wu staffs, and six each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, star-emblems, and battle-axes.
translations.idiomatic: Next came six imperial staffs, six wu staffs, and six each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, star-maces, and battle-axes.

sentences.zh: 次五色金龍小旗十，五色龍纛十。

translations.literal: Next ten small five-colored golden-dragon flags and ten five-colored dragon banners.
translations.idiomatic: Next came ten small five-colored golden-dragon flags and ten five-colored dragon banners.

sentences.zh: 次單龍赤團扇六，雙龍黃團扇六，五色花傘十。

translations.literal: Next six single-dragon red round fans, six double-dragon yellow round fans, and ten five-colored floral umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: Six single-dragon red round fans, six double-dragon yellow round fans, and ten five-colored floral umbrellas followed.

sentences.zh: 次豹尾槍十，弓矢十，儀刀十。

translations.literal: Next ten leopard-tail spears, ten bows and arrows, and ten ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Next came ten leopard-tail spears, ten bows and arrows, and ten ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 次九龍曲柄黃華蓋一。

translations.literal: Next one curved-handle yellow nine-dragon splendor canopy.
translations.idiomatic: One curved-handle yellow nine-dragon splendor canopy came next.

sentences.zh: 皆在皇帝輕步輿前，若乘馬則在馬前。

translations.literal: All were before the emperor's light walking palanquin; if he rode a horse, they were before the horse.
translations.idiomatic: All of these preceded the emperor's light walking palanquin, or his horse when he rode.

sentences.zh: 次前引佩刀大臣十人，後扈佩刀大臣二人，輕步輿在中。

translations.idiomatic: One red silk umbrella embroidered with baoxiang flowers and two blue silk fans embroidered with baoxiang flowers were included.

translations.idiomatic: On ordinary days no attendants led in front; only two followed behind.

sentences.zh: 餘官均用青素扇一。

translations.literal: All remaining officials used one plain blue fan.
translations.idiomatic: All lower-ranking officials used one plain blue fan.

sentences.zh: 常日惟後從一人。

translations.literal: On ordinary days only one followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: On ordinary days only one attendant followed behind.

sentences.zh: 宗室、覺羅之有職者，各從其品，惟扇柄及棍皆魨以硃。

translations.literal: Members of the imperial clan and gioro who held office each followed their rank, but both fan handles and sticks were coated with cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and gioro in office followed their rank in other respects, but fan handles and sticks were lacquered in cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 以上儀衛，於京外得全設，常日在京，不得用旗、傘、黃棍。

translations.literal: The ceremonial guards listed above might be fully deployed outside the capital; on ordinary days in the capital flags, umbrellas, and yellow sticks were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The above ceremonial guards could be fully deployed outside the capital, but on ordinary days within Beijing flags, umbrellas, and yellow sticks were prohibited.

sentences.zh: 文官三品以上，得用甘蔗棍二。

translations.literal: Civil officials of third rank and above might use two sugarcane sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of third rank and above might employ two sugarcane sticks.

sentences.zh: 武官三品以上，得用棕竹棍二。

translations.literal: Military officials of third rank and above might use two palm-bamboo sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials of third rank and above might employ two palm-bamboo sticks.

sentences.zh: 自一品至九品，均得用扇，扇各用清、漢字書銜。

translations.literal: From first to ninth rank all might use fans; each fan bore the title in both Manchu and Chinese characters.
translations.idiomatic: From first through ninth rank all might carry fans inscribed with their titles in both Manchu and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 若進皇城，扇棍及前引人均不得入。

translations.literal: If entering the Imperial City, fans, sticks, and those leading in front were all not permitted to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering the Imperial City, fans, sticks, and front attendants were all barred from entry.

sentences.zh: 文武大臣因事入景運門，帶從官一人。

translations.literal: When civil and military grand ministers entered Jingyun Gate on business, they might bring one attending official.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military grand ministers entering Jingyun Gate on official business might be accompanied by one attendant.

sentences.zh: 直省文官，總督，青旗八，飛虎旗、杏黃傘、青扇、兵拳、雁翎刀、獸劍、金黃棍、桐棍、皮槊各二，旗槍四，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Civil officials of the provinces: a governor-general—eight blue flags; two each of flying-tiger flags, apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, military fists, goose-feather sabers, ceremonial swords, golden-yellow sticks, paulownia sticks, and leather spears; four flag spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Among provincial civil officials, a governor-general received eight blue flags; two each of flying-tiger flags, apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, military fists, goose-feather sabers, ceremonial swords, golden-yellow sticks, paulownia sticks, and leather spears; four flag spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 巡撫，青旗八，杏黃傘、青扇、獸劍、金黃棍、桐棍、皮槊各二、旗槍二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: A governor: eight blue flags; two each of apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, ceremonial swords, golden-yellow sticks, paulownia sticks, and leather spears; two flag spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: A governor received eight blue flags; two each of apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, ceremonial swords, golden-yellow sticks, paulownia sticks, and leather spears; two flag spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 凡二品以上大臣陛見到京，入景運門，帶從官一人。

translations.literal: Whenever grand ministers of second rank and above came to the capital for imperial audience and entered Jingyun Gate, they might bring one attending official.
translations.idiomatic: Grand ministers of second rank and above who came to the capital for audience and entered Jingyun Gate might be accompanied by one attendant.

sentences.zh: 布政使、按察使，青旗六，杏黃傘、青扇、金黃棍、皮槊各二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Financial and judicial commissioners: six blue flags; two each of apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, golden-yellow sticks, and leather spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Financial and judicial commissioners received six blue flags; two each of apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, golden-yellow sticks, and leather spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 各道青旗四，杏黃傘、青扇各一，桐棍、皮槊各二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Circuit intendants: four blue flags; one each of apricot-yellow umbrella and blue fan; two each of paulownia sticks and leather spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendants received four blue flags; one apricot-yellow umbrella and one blue fan; two paulownia sticks and two leather spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 知府與道同。

translations.literal: Prefects were the same as circuit intendants.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects received the same ceremonial guard as circuit intendants.

sentences.zh: 府倅、知州、知縣，青旗四，藍傘一，青扇一，桐棍、皮槊各二，肅靜牌二。

translations.literal: Assistant prefects, department magistrates, and county magistrates: four blue flags, one blue umbrella, one blue fan, two each of paulownia sticks and leather spears, and two silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant prefects, department magistrates, and county magistrates received four blue flags, one blue umbrella, one blue fan, two paulownia sticks, two leather spears, and two silence placards.

sentences.zh: 縣佐，藍傘一，桐棍二。

translations.literal: Assistant county magistrates: one blue umbrella and two paulownia sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant county magistrates received one blue umbrella and two paulownia sticks.

sentences.zh: 學官，藍傘一。

translations.literal: Educational officials: one blue umbrella.
translations.idiomatic: Educational officials received one blue umbrella.

sentences.zh: 雜職，竹板二。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous officials: two bamboo boards.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous officials received two bamboo boards.

sentences.zh: 河道、漕運總督視總督，學政、鹽政、織造暨各欽差官三品以上視巡撫。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators of rivers and grain transport ranked with a governor-general; educational commissioners, salt commissioners, textile commissioners, and all imperial commissioners of third rank and above ranked with a governor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators of rivers and grain transport ranked with a governor-general, while educational commissioners, salt commissioners, textile commissioners, and imperial commissioners of third rank and above ranked with a governor.

sentences.zh: 四品以下視兩司。

translations.literal: Fourth rank and below ranked with the two commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fourth rank and below ranked with the financial and judicial commissioners.

sentences.zh: 武官，提督，青旗八，飛虎旗、杏黃傘、青扇、兵拳、雁翎刀、獸劍、刑仗各二，旗槍四，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Military officials: a provincial commander-in-chief—eight blue flags; two each of flying-tiger flags, apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, military fists, goose-feather sabers, ceremonial swords, and punishment staffs; four flag spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Among military officials, a provincial commander-in-chief received eight blue flags; two each of flying-tiger flags, apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, military fists, goose-feather sabers, ceremonial swords, and punishment staffs; four flag spears; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 總兵官，青旗八，飛虎旗、杏黃傘、青扇、獸劍、旗槍、大刀各二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Regional commanders: eight blue flags; two each of flying-tiger flags, apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, ceremonial swords, flag spears, and broadswords; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders received eight blue flags; two each of flying-tiger flags, apricot-yellow umbrellas, blue fans, ceremonial swords, flag spears, and broadswords; and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 副將，青旗六，杏黃傘一，青扇二，金黃棍二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Brigadier generals: six blue flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, two blue fans, two golden-yellow sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Brigadier generals received six blue flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, two blue fans, two golden-yellow sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 參將、游擊、都司，青旗四，杏黃傘一，青扇一，桐棍二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Colonels, brigade commanders, and garrison commanders: four blue flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, one blue fan, two paulownia sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Colonels, brigade commanders, and garrison commanders received four blue flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, one blue fan, two paulownia sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 守備，青旗四，杏黃傘一，青扇一，桐棍二。

translations.literal: Fortress commanders: four blue flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, one blue fan, and two paulownia sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Fortress commanders received four blue flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, one blue fan, and two paulownia sticks.

sentences.zh: 各省駐防將軍視內都統。

translations.literal: Garrison generals of the provinces ranked with metropolitan banner vice commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial garrison generals ranked with metropolitan banner vice commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 副都統以下均與京職同。

translations.literal: From vice commander-in-chief downward all matched capital appointments.
translations.idiomatic: From vice commander-in-chief downward all matched the capital establishment.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，定京官儀從，公，掌扇貼方金一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, capital officials' ceremonial retinue was fixed: for a duke, one official fan with square gold appliqué.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi the court fixed the ceremonial retinue of capital officials: a duke received one official fan bearing a square gold appliqué.

sentences.zh: 職官掌扇，一品貼圓金四，二品貼圓金三，三品貼圓金二，四品用灑金掌扇，五品至七品俱用素黑掌扇，八品、九品俱用白掌扇。

translations.literal: Officials' ceremonial fans: first rank bore four round gold appliqués, second rank three, third rank two; fourth rank used gold-sprinkled official fans; fifth through seventh ranks all used plain black official fans; eighth and ninth ranks all used white official fans.
translations.idiomatic: For officials' ceremonial fans, first rank bore four round gold appliqués, second rank three, and third rank two; fourth rank used gold-sprinkled fans; fifth through seventh ranks used plain black fans; and eighth and ninth ranks used white fans.

sentences.zh: 六年，定公以下四品官以上用大、小灑金扇各一，文官用甘蔗棍二，武官用棕竹棍二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year it was fixed that from duke downward officials of fourth rank and above used one each of large and small gold-sprinkled fans; civil officials used two sugarcane sticks and military officials two palm-bamboo sticks.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the court ruled that from duke downward officials of fourth rank and above carried one large and one small gold-sprinkled fan; civil officials employed two sugarcane sticks and military officials two palm-bamboo sticks.

sentences.zh: 八年，定民公、和碩公主額駙，杏黃傘二，旗十，大、小扇二，貼方金四。

translations.literal: In the eighth year it was fixed for a commoner duke and an imperial son-in-law of a Princess of Harmonious Solemnity: two apricot-yellow umbrellas, ten flags, two large and small fans, and four square gold appliqués.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year a commoner duke and an imperial son-in-law of a Princess of Harmonious Solemnity were allotted two apricot-yellow umbrellas, ten flags, two large and small fans, and four square gold appliqués.

sentences.zh: 侯、郡主額駙，杏黃傘一，旗十，大、小扇二，貼方金三。

translations.literal: A marquis and an imperial son-in-law of a commandery princess: one apricot-yellow umbrella, ten flags, two large and small fans, and three square gold appliqués.
translations.idiomatic: A marquis and an imperial son-in-law of a commandery princess received one apricot-yellow umbrella, ten flags, two large and small fans, and three square gold appliqués.

sentences.zh: 伯，杏黃傘一，旗十，大、小扇二，貼圓金一。

translations.literal: An earl: one apricot-yellow umbrella, ten flags, two large and small fans, and one round gold appliqué.
translations.idiomatic: An earl received one apricot-yellow umbrella, ten flags, two large and small fans, and one round gold appliqué.

sentences.zh: 一品官，杏黃傘一，旗八，大、小扇二，貼圓金四。

translations.literal: A first-rank official: one apricot-yellow umbrella, eight flags, two large and small fans, and four round gold appliqués.
translations.idiomatic: A first-rank official received one apricot-yellow umbrella, eight flags, two large and small fans, and four round gold appliqués.

sentences.zh: 二品官，杏黃傘一，旗六，大、小扇二，貼圓金三。

translations.literal: A second-rank official: one apricot-yellow umbrella, six flags, two large and small fans, and three round gold appliqués.
translations.idiomatic: A second-rank official received one apricot-yellow umbrella, six flags, two large and small fans, and three round gold appliqués.

sentences.zh: 三品官，杏黃傘一，旗六，大、小扇二，貼圓金二。

translations.literal: A third-rank official: one apricot-yellow umbrella, six flags, two large and small fans, and two round gold appliqués.
translations.idiomatic: A third-rank official received one apricot-yellow umbrella, six flags, two large and small fans, and two round gold appliqués.

sentences.zh: 四品官，旗四，灑金大、小扇二。

translations.literal: A fourth-rank official: four flags and two large and small gold-sprinkled fans.
translations.idiomatic: A fourth-rank official received four flags and two large and small gold-sprinkled fans.

sentences.zh: 五品以下官如三年例。

translations.literal: Officials of fifth rank and below followed the third-year precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and below followed the regulations of the third year.

sentences.zh: 京城內不得排列旗、傘，惟於外用之。

translations.literal: Within the capital city flags and umbrellas might not be arrayed; they were used only outside.
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital flags and umbrellas might not be displayed; they were permitted only outside the city.

sentences.zh: 宗室、覺羅各官，扇柄及棍皆丹漆。

translations.literal: All officials among the imperial clan and gioro had fan handles and sticks lacquered in cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and gioro officials lacquered both fan handles and sticks in cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 凡入皇城，惟用小扇。

translations.literal: Upon entering the Imperial City only small fans were used.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering the Imperial City only small fans might be carried.

sentences.zh: 九年，定公以下、漢文官三品以上，皇城外坐暗轎，四人舁之，掌扇各書官銜，兼滿、漢字。

translations.literal: In the ninth year it was fixed that from duke downward and Han civil officials of third rank and above, outside the Imperial City sat in closed sedan chairs borne by four bearers; official fans each bore the office title in both Manchu and Chinese characters.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the court ruled that from duke downward and Han civil officials of third rank and above traveled outside the Imperial City in closed sedan chairs carried by four bearers, with ceremonial fans inscribed in both Manchu and Chinese with their titles.

sentences.zh: 康熙初年，定公、和碩公主額駙，旗十，杏黃傘二，金黃棍四。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi years it was fixed for a duke and an imperial son-in-law of a Princess of Harmonious Solemnity: ten flags, two apricot-yellow umbrellas, and four golden-yellow sticks.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kangxi era a duke and an imperial son-in-law of a Princess of Harmonious Solemnity received ten flags, two apricot-yellow umbrellas, and four golden-yellow sticks.

sentences.zh: 侯、伯、郡主額駙，旗十，杏黃傘一，金黃棍四。

translations.literal: A marquis, earl, and imperial son-in-law of a commandery princess: ten flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, and four golden-yellow sticks.
translations.idiomatic: A marquis, earl, and imperial son-in-law of a commandery princess received ten flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, and four golden-yellow sticks.

sentences.zh: 都統，鎮國將軍，內大臣，縣主額駙，子，滿、漢大學士，尚書，左都御史，旗八，杏黃傘一，金黃棍二。

translations.literal: Banner commanders-in-chief, defenders of the state generals, inner grand ministers, imperial sons-in-law of county princesses, viscounts, Manchu and Han grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief: eight flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, and two golden-yellow sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Banner commanders-in-chief, defenders of the state generals, inner grand ministers, imperial sons-in-law of county princesses, viscounts, Manchu and Han grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief received eight flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, and two golden-yellow sticks.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍，郡君額駙，護軍統領，前鋒統領，副都統，男，滿、漢侍郎，學士，步軍總尉及三品官，旗六，杏黃傘一，金黃棍二。

translations.literal: Bulwark-of-the-state generals, imperial sons-in-law of commandery ladies, commanders of the Guard, commanders of the Vanguard, vice commanders-in-chief, barons, Manchu and Han vice ministers, academicians, commandant of the Metropolitan Infantry, and third-rank officials: six flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, and two golden-yellow sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Bulwark-of-the-state generals, imperial sons-in-law of commandery ladies, commanders of the Guard and Vanguard, vice commanders-in-chief, barons, Manchu and Han vice ministers, academicians, the commandant of the Metropolitan Infantry, and third-rank officials received six flags, one apricot-yellow umbrella, and two golden-yellow sticks.

sentences.zh: 四品官旗四。

translations.literal: Fourth-rank officials: four flags.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank officials received four flags.

sentences.zh: 京城內一品官以上惟用傘、棍，二品官並不用傘。

translations.literal: Within the capital first-rank officials and above used only umbrellas and sticks; second-rank officials did not use umbrellas at all.
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital first-rank officials and above might carry only umbrellas and sticks, and second-rank officials might not use umbrellas at all.

sentences.zh: 四年，定在京文官三品以上、武官散秩大臣以上，一人引馬前導，其餘各官禁之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year it was fixed that in the capital civil officials of third rank and above and military officials of minister-without-portfolio rank and above might have one man lead a horse in front as guide; all other officials were forbidden this.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the court ruled that in the capital civil officials of third rank and above and senior military ministers without portfolio might be preceded by one horse guide, while all other officials were forbidden the practice.

sentences.zh: 七年，定在京各官停用傘、棍，民公以下俱照順治八年例，出京用鞍籠閒馬前導。

translations.literal: In the seventh year it was fixed that all capital officials ceased using umbrellas and sticks; from commoner duke downward all followed the eighth-year Shunzhi precedent, using saddle-caged spare horses as guides when leaving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the court abolished umbrellas and sticks for all capital officials; from commoner duke downward all followed the Shunzhi eighth-year regulations, employing saddle-caged spare horses as outriders when traveling outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，定外官儀從。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi, the ceremonial retinue of outside officials was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kangxi the court fixed the ceremonial retinue of provincial officials.

sentences.zh: 總督，杏黃傘二，金黃棍二，旗八，扇二，兵拳二，雁翎刀二，飛虎旗二，獸劍二，桐棍二，槊棍二，槍四，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: A governor-general: two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, eight flags, two fans, two military fists, two goose-feather sabers, two flying-tiger flags, two ceremonial swords, two paulownia sticks, two spear-sticks, four spears, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: A governor-general received two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, eight flags, two fans, two military fists, two goose-feather sabers, two flying-tiger flags, two ceremonial swords, two paulownia sticks, two spear-sticks, four spears, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 巡撫，杏黃傘二，金黃棍二，旗八，扇二，獸劍二，桐棍二，槊棍二，槍二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: A governor: two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, eight flags, two fans, two ceremonial swords, two paulownia sticks, two spear-sticks, two spears, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: A governor received two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, eight flags, two fans, two ceremonial swords, two paulownia sticks, two spear-sticks, two spears, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 布政使、按察使，杏黃傘二，金黃棍二，旗六，扇二，槊棍二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Financial and judicial commissioners: two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, six flags, two fans, two spear-sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Financial and judicial commissioners received two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, six flags, two fans, two spear-sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 各道掌印、都司、知府，杏黃傘一，旗四，桐棍二，槊棍二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Circuit seal-holders, regional commanders, and prefects: one apricot-yellow umbrella, four flags, two paulownia sticks, two spear-sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit seal-holders, regional commanders, and prefects received one apricot-yellow umbrella, four flags, two paulownia sticks, two spear-sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 同知、通判、知州、知縣，藍傘一，扇一，桐棍一，槊棍一，迴避牌二。

translations.literal: Vice prefects, subprefects, department magistrates, and county magistrates: one blue umbrella, one fan, one paulownia stick, one spear-stick, and two avoidance placards.
translations.idiomatic: Vice prefects, subprefects, department magistrates, and county magistrates received one blue umbrella, one fan, one paulownia stick, one spear-stick, and two avoidance placards.

sentences.zh: 州同、州判、縣丞，藍傘一，桐棍二。

translations.literal: Department assistants, department judges, and county assistants: one blue umbrella and two paulownia sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Department assistants, department judges, and county assistants received one blue umbrella and two paulownia sticks.

sentences.zh: 典史、雜職，竹板二。

translations.literal: Petty officials and miscellaneous posts: two bamboo boards.
translations.idiomatic: Petty officials and miscellaneous posts were allowed two bamboo boards.

sentences.zh: 提督，杏黃傘二，金黃棍二，旗八，扇二，兵拳二，雁翎刀二，飛虎旗二，槍二，獸劍二，刑仗二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Provincial military governors: two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, eight flags, two fans, two military fists, two goose-quill sabers, two flying-tiger flags, two spears, two beast swords, two punishment staffs, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial military governors received two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, eight flags, two fans, two military fists, two goose-quill sabers, two flying-tiger flags, two spears, two beast swords, two punishment staffs, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 總兵，杏黃傘二，金黃棍二，旗八，扇二，大刀一，獸劍二，槍二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Regional commanders: two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, eight flags, two fans, one great sword, two beast swords, two spears, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders received two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, eight flags, two fans, one great sword, two beast swords, two spears, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 副將，杏黃傘二，金黃棍二，旗六，扇二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Deputy commanders: two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, six flags, two fans, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commanders received two apricot-yellow umbrellas, two golden-yellow sticks, six flags, two fans, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 參將、游擊、都司，杏黃傘一，旗四，扇一，桐棍二，迴避、肅靜牌各二。

translations.literal: Brigade generals, mobile detachment commanders, and regional commanders: one apricot-yellow umbrella, four flags, one fan, two paulownia sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade generals, mobile detachment commanders, and regional commanders received one apricot-yellow umbrella, four flags, one fan, two paulownia sticks, and two each of avoidance and silence placards.

sentences.zh: 守備，杏黃傘一，旗四，扇一，棍二。

translations.literal: Garrison commanders: one apricot-yellow umbrella, four flags, one fan, and two sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commanders received one apricot-yellow umbrella, four flags, one fan, and two sticks.

sentences.zh: 崇德初年，定固倫額駙，彩畫雲紅傘一，豹尾槍二，紅仗二。

translations.literal: In the early Chongde years it was fixed for an imperial son-in-law of an imperial princess of the first rank: one cloud-painted red umbrella, two leopard-tail spears, and two red staffs.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chongde years the court fixed for an imperial son-in-law of an imperial princess of the first rank one cloud-painted red umbrella, two leopard-tail spears, and two red staffs.

sentences.zh: 超品公、和碩額駙，金黃傘一，豹尾槍二，旗六，後從十人。

translations.literal: A supra-rank duke and an imperial son-in-law of a princess of the second rank: one golden-yellow umbrella, two leopard-tail spears, six flags, and ten attendants following behind.
translations.idiomatic: A supra-rank duke and an imperial son-in-law of a princess of the second rank received one golden-yellow umbrella, two leopard-tail spears, six flags, and ten attendants in the rear.

sentences.zh: 民公、郡主額駙，金黃傘一，豹尾槍一，旗六，後從八人。

translations.literal: A Han duke and an imperial son-in-law of a commandery princess: one golden-yellow umbrella, one leopard-tail spear, six flags, and eight attendants following behind.
translations.idiomatic: A Han duke and an imperial son-in-law of a commandery princess received one golden-yellow umbrella, one leopard-tail spear, six flags, and eight attendants in the rear.

sentences.zh: 都統、子、尚書、縣主額駙，金黃傘一，旗六，後從六人。

translations.literal: A banner commander, viscount, minister of a ministry, and imperial son-in-law of a county princess: one golden-yellow umbrella, six flags, and six attendants following behind.
translations.idiomatic: A banner commander, viscount, minister of a ministry, and imperial son-in-law of a county princess received one golden-yellow umbrella, six flags, and six attendants in the rear.

sentences.zh: 內大臣、大學士、副都統、護軍統領、前鋒統領、侍郎、郡君額駙，旗六，後從四人。

translations.literal: An inner grand minister, grand secretary, deputy banner commander, guard-army commander, vanguard commander, vice minister, and imperial son-in-law of a commandery lady: six flags and four attendants following behind.
translations.idiomatic: An inner grand minister, grand secretary, deputy banner commander, guard-army commander, vanguard commander, vice minister, and imperial son-in-law of a commandery lady received six flags and four attendants in the rear.

sentences.zh: 一等侍衛、護衛、參領、前鋒參領、縣君額駙、學士、滿啟心郎、郎中，旗四，後從四人。

translations.literal: A first-class guard, bodyguard, company commander, vanguard company commander, imperial son-in-law of a county lady, academician, Manchu qinxinlang, and department director: four flags and four attendants following behind.
translations.idiomatic: A first-class guard, bodyguard, company commander, vanguard company commander, imperial son-in-law of a county lady, academician, Manchu qinxinlang, and department director received four flags and four attendants in the rear.

sentences.zh: 二等侍衛、護衛、佐領、漢啟心郎、員外郎，旗二，後從二人。

translations.literal: A second-class guard, bodyguard, assistant company commander, Han qinxinlang, and vice director: two flags and two attendants following behind.
translations.idiomatic: A second-class guard, bodyguard, assistant company commander, Han qinxinlang, and vice director received two flags and two attendants in the rear.

sentences.zh: 三等侍衛、護衛、護軍校、主事以下官員，止用後從一人。

translations.literal: Third-class guards, bodyguards, guard-army officers, and officials from secretary and below used only one attendant following behind.
translations.idiomatic: Third-class guards, bodyguards, guard-army officers, and officials from secretary downward were limited to a single attendant in the rear.
